name: Once the In2S3/CNGS interface defect density exceeds about 10^16 cm^-2, increasing interfacial traps enhances SRH recombination, lowers minority-carrier lifetime and extraction efficiency, reduces qua
description: Once the In2S3/CNGS interface defect density exceeds about 10^16 cm^-2, increasing interfacial traps enhances SRH recombination, lowers minority-carrier lifetime and extraction efficiency, reduces quasi-Fermi-level splitting, and thereby decreases VOC, JSC, FF, and PCE.
evidence_span: Once the defect density exceeds 1016 cm-2, all photovoltaic parameters gradually decrease. The increasing density of interfacial traps enhances SRH recombination at the In2S3/CNGS junction, reducing the minority-carrier lifetime and increasing carrier losses during the extraction process. As a result, the quasi-Fermi level splitting decreases, leading to a reduction in VOC, while the diminished carrier collection efficiency lowers JSC. The combined impact of these losses results in a gradual degradation of FF and overall device efficiency.

evidence_span: These results indicate that the proposed device is relatively insensitive to moderate variations in intrinsic recombination coefficients but becomes increasingly susceptible once the corresponding recombination rates become comparable to the carrier extraction rate.

evidence_span: Elevated temperature increases carrier scattering and recombination rates, which reduce carrier lifetime and degrade transport efficiency. In addition, the weakening of the built-in electric field at higher temperatures reduces carrier separation efficiency, leading to increased resistive and recombination losses. These effects collectively result in a deterioration of the current–voltage characteristics and a reduction in FF.

description: The slight VOC increase associated with neutral defects should be interpreted not as stronger built-in field, but as a model-dependent self-consistent consequence of carrier populations, defect occupation, and recombination under open-circuit conditions.
evidence_span: Because the defects considered here are electrically neutral, the slight increase in VOC should not be attributed to defect-induced enhancement of the built-in electric field or junction electrostatics. Rather, it is more appropriately regarded as a modest model-dependent response arising from the self-consistent interplay among carrier populations, defect occupation, and recombination under open-circuit conditions.

name: Increasing defect density lowers SRH lifetime and minority-carrier diffusion length, making photocarriers less likely to reach charge-selective interfaces before recombining; this increases defect-ass
description: Increasing defect density lowers SRH lifetime and minority-carrier diffusion length, making photocarriers less likely to reach charge-selective interfaces before recombining; this increases defect-assisted recombination, degrades illuminated J-V behavior, reduces JSC, and lowers the maximum extractable power.
evidence_span: As the defect concentration increases, the carrier lifetime decreases, leading to a reduction in the minority-carrier diffusion length... The resulting reduction in carrier lifetime and diffusion length lowers the probability that photogenerated carriers reach the charge-selective interfaces before recombination. Consequently, a larger fraction of carriers recombines within the CNGS absorber, resulting in a progressive reduction in current collection efficiency and a corresponding decline in JSC.

name: At low front-interface defect density, the built-in field separates photogenerated carriers before trap capture; at the rear interface, defects create recombination pathways for electrons and holes th
description: At low front-interface defect density, the built-in field separates photogenerated carriers before trap capture; at the rear interface, defects create recombination pathways for electrons and holes that reduce carrier collection and quasi-Fermi-level splitting, and once defect density becomes high the device enters a recombination-limited regime where further trap increases have little additional effect. These rear-interface defects mainly increase recombination rather than transport resistance, so voltage and photocurrent fall while J-V shape changes little.
evidence_span: At low interface defect densities, the built-in electric field efficiently separates photogenerated carriers before they can be captured by interfacial trap states.

name: Radiative recombination is a minor loss mechanism at low radiative coefficients because carriers are collected before recombining, whereas Auger recombination is inherently more sensitive because it i
description: Radiative recombination is a minor loss mechanism at low radiative coefficients because carriers are collected before recombining, whereas Auger recombination is inherently more sensitive because it is a three-particle process that scales strongly with carrier density.
evidence_span: At relatively small values of the radiative recombination coefficient, this process constitutes only a minor fraction of the total carrier-loss mechanism, allowing photogenerated carriers to be efficiently separated and collected before recombination occurs.

name: Temperature affects performance through competing trap/recombination processes: rising temperature increases reverse saturation current via thermally activated generation and stronger SRH recombinatio
description: Temperature affects performance through competing trap/recombination processes: rising temperature increases reverse saturation current via thermally activated generation and stronger SRH recombination, which reduces quasi-Fermi-level splitting and VOC; at higher temperature, thermally assisted detrapping can partially offset recombination losses and modestly recover photocurrent.
evidence_span: This behavior arises from the temperature dependence of the reverse saturation current density, which increases due to enhanced thermally activated carrier generation and increased SRH recombination. As temperature rises, the probability of carrier occupation of higher energy states increases, leading to stronger recombination activity and a reduction in quasi-Fermi level splitting. Consequently, VOC continuously degrades with temperature.

name: Under stronger illumination, photogeneration and carrier density rise, increasing quasi-Fermi-level splitting; however, because recombination also grows with carrier concentration, VOC increases sub-l
description: Under stronger illumination, photogeneration and carrier density rise, increasing quasi-Fermi-level splitting; however, because recombination also grows with carrier concentration, VOC increases sub-linearly, while JSC remains nearly linear because photogeneration scales with photon flux and collection efficiency stays relatively stable. Higher illumination also strengthens carrier extraction and drift-assisted transport, reducing the relative impact of series resistance and improving FF.
evidence_span: As illumination increases, the photogenerated carrier density rises, leading to an increase in quasi-Fermi level splitting. However, because recombination processes also increase with carrier concentration, the growth of VOC follows a sub-linear, logarithmic trend rather than a linear one.

name: In the spatial extension, synthetic identifiability tests show several spatial features are recoverable, but the in-layer defect-transport composition gradient—the key extra spatial quantity—is weakly
description: In the spatial extension, synthetic identifiability tests show several spatial features are recoverable, but the in-layer defect-transport composition gradient—the key extra spatial quantity—is weakly identifiable.
evidence_span: Twenty replicate synthetic experiments (SI, Table S7) show that the barrier-layer thickness, interfacial transition widths, nickel-zone amplitude and width, and in-layer chromium fraction are identifiable (replicate relative standard deviations 2–19%), while the in-layer defect-transport composition gradient, the one quantity the spatial extension uniquely adds, is weak (47%, with a minimum statistically detectable gradient of 0.93 absolute weight percent across the layer).

name: Nickel-zone closure and mobility variants fail: a constant-mobility nickel-transport model is rejected by the data (χ2 = 25.7 on 1 dof) because measured nickel-zone widths remain roughly flat across a
description: Nickel-zone closure and mobility variants fail: a constant-mobility nickel-transport model is rejected by the data (χ2 = 25.7 on 1 dof) because measured nickel-zone widths remain roughly flat across a 6.7× exposure-time increase instead of growing as sqrt(time) or faster; two physically motivated one-parameter nickel-zone extensions also fail a synthetic identifiability gate, and a forward-only scan finds no flux-coupled parameter value that is both shape-correct and quantitatively improved.
evidence_span: An exact moving-frame nickel-transport model with a constant effective mobility ... is rejected by the data: χ2 = 25.7 on one degree of freedom.
